messages:
mike: nightly-alert: 03:12 UTC failing schema checks for fncall outputs on open-m-3b-q4 run. stack of parse errors from eval harness. anyone seen this pattern before?
nightly-bot: nightly-eval open-m-3b-q4 | suite: toolcall-integration | failures: 12 | first_fail: 1849123456
zara: can you paste the raw model output for one failing prompt? sounds like the parser choked on a field again.
mike: pasted below — this is the function output captured by eval harness (trimmed):
```
{"tool": "send_batch", "args": "{\"recipient_ids\": \"[1023,2048]\", \"priority\": \"normal\"}"}
```
mike: note `args` is a string containing JSON. our fncall schema expects args to be an object. validator throws: UnexpectedType: expected object, got string.
samira: hmm, that looks like double-serialization. is the runtime wrapping args as a string on some code path? only seen this after we switched to q4 quant build for this model.
bert: I ran a repro locally with the same model binary (open-m-3b-q4) and got similar outputs. when using the non-quant baseline (open-m-3b) the args come through as proper JSON object.
zara: do you have the seed + prompt that reproduces?
burt: (I assume you meant bert) the failing prompt is in nightly bundle: /evals/promptsets/send_batch_edgecases.json, test case #7. seed 42. command: `python infra/evals/run_nightly.py --model open-m-3b-q4 --case send_batch_edgecases --seed 42`
mike: repro steps confirmed. attaching minimal stdout:
```
...generation start...
ToolCall: send_batch({"recipient_ids":"[1023,2048]","priority":"normal"})\n...generation end...
```
mike: notice ToolCall printed as function with args wrapped in quotes.
samira: could be tokenization producing extra escapes around braces/quotes, or our postprocessor mistakenly `json.dumps`ing args again for broadcasting.
zara: quick check — is this only for arrays inside args? or any nested object?
mike: also saw a case where numeric ids came out as `"00123"` (leading zeros preserved) vs baseline `123`. so two separate issues: stringified JSON blob and id formatting.
bert: I dumped the model's raw logits-to-text path and saw the generator emitting an extra `\"` sequence before the opening `{` in some samples. looks like the model learned to emit escaped quotes for safety?
samira: that points to decoding/tokenization differences between quant and baseline. q4 packing changes byte-to-token mapping for some bytes sequences; if our detokenizer or beam postprocessor treats bytes differently we could end up with extra backslashes.
zara: next steps: 1) run localized eval with `--emit-raw` to get exact token ids 2) run detokenize using both our runtime detok and a reference detok to see divergence 3) add a short schema-rescue step in eval harness to detect stringified-json and attempt parse as fallback (log as warning) so nightly alerts don't spam SRE.
mike: I'll pick up 1+2. running now, will post token ids.
bert: I'll trace the runtime code path that wraps fncall args — search for `serialize_args` in runtime v1.8. might be an accidental extra `encode(json.dumps(...))` when model is flagged quantized.
samira: good. also let's try generating with `--no-safety-escape` knob in the runtime (exists for debugging) to see if escaping behavior changes.
zara: if we confirm it's quantization-detokenizer mismatch, we should gate the q4 build from nightly until fixed or add a conversion shim in the serving runtime.
mike: quick note: putting a rescue parse in eval harness temporarily reduces alerts and gives us more triage time. I'll open a PR to catch args as string and attempt json.loads; will annotate with failing_model and tokens.
mike: PR draft: `evals/validators/fncall_fix.py` — naive fallback: if type(args)==str: try json.loads(args); if fails raise.
samira: fine as short-term. but add a metric tag so we can count how many fallbacks happen per-model.
bert: assigned runtime investigation to me. I'll post findings by EOD. tagging @samira for infra follow-up. :eyes:
zara: thanks team. please post token dumps here when ready so we can decide rollback vs shim. :thumbsup:
